skills.name: premium-3d-models
skills.description: Build real, parametric 3D models (.glb primarily, plus .stl/.obj on request) for any use case that ends up embedding, printing, or viewing 3D geometry — a Flutter app's model_viewer_plus screen, a React/web page with model-viewer or react-three-fiber, a part imported into Blender for further work, or a file ready for a 3D printer. Use this whenever the user asks to "model," "3D model," "make a 3D object/part/ asset of," or describes a mechanical part, product shape, prop, or sculptural object that should exist as real geometry rather than a 2D image. Two working styles this skill switches between: an "engineer" persona (exact dimensions, holes, tolerances, mechanical parts) and a "designer" persona (organic/sculptural silhouettes, materials, product form). If the use case or style is not obvious from the request, ask briefly (see Step 1) instead of guessing a persona or output format.

skills.name: premium-presentations
skills.description: Build fully editable, professional/premium presentations (and the same quality bar for documents, spreadsheets, and PDFs) — not flat images, not generic template filler. Use this whenever the user asks for a presentation, slide deck, pitch deck, investor deck, PowerPoint, keynote, or any "make me slides about X" request, even if they don't say "professional" or "premium" explicitly — treat every deck request as wanting agency-quality output unless they clearly say otherwise (e.g. "just a rough draft"). If the user hasn't specified a visual style/theme, ALWAYS stop and ask them (see "Step 1: figure out the design" below) instead of guessing — a wrong visual direction is expensive to redo, a quick question is not. Also use this skill's methodology (deck-spec to native-format generation, ask-before-guessing on design, real data not placeholders) as the pattern for sibling skills that build documents or spreadsheets to the same premium bar.

skills.name: premium-subtitle-localization
skills.description: Add translated subtitles to a video — find or generate source-language subtitles, translate them with real cultural/comedic adaptation (never a flat literal translation), validate formatting and timing, and mux the result into the video without re-encoding. Use this whenever the user asks to subtitle, translate, localize, or dub (subtitle-only) a video/movie/show into another language, or gives a video file and a target language. Involves a "virtual expert team" of translation passes (literal draft, meaning-preserving rewrite, cultural adaptation, fluency/timing polish) plus automated QA and an agentic review pass — not a single mechanical translate-and-burn-in step. Also verifies the source transcript against the actual audio before translating, so dialect/ASR errors are caught rather than silently rewritten into fluent invented dialogue.

skills.name: skill-enhancer
skills.description: Audits and improves any skill in this repo using real usage reports (or a direct read-through when none exist yet) — finds recurring issues, missing coverage, and rough edges, fixes them, re-validates, and ships the update. Use when a skill produced a bad/wrong/incomplete result and should be fixed, when asked to "enhance"/"improve"/"audit" a skill, when asked to review skill quality or performance, or periodically to process accumulated usage reports. Also defines the reporting mechanism itself (skill-router logs a report after every skill use) that feeds this.

skills.name: skill-router
skills.description: Read this FIRST, before any other skill, for any non-trivial request — it is the dispatcher for every skill in this repo. Checks skills/manifest.json and auto-selects a matching installed skill with no need to ask the user which one to use. If nothing installed matches, searches for or builds a new skill and installs it into this repo automatically (clone/build for the user's own MCP repos, or build from scratch via the skill-creator methodology), then tells the user what was added. Also covers keeping skills/manifest.json in sync as skills are added or changed.
